data.long_meaning: The name Mehndi originates from the Arabic word for 'henna', a plant used for temporary body art. In Muslim culture, applying henna is a symbolic act of love, commitment, and blessings for the bride before her wedding. The name Mehndi carries the meaning “Henna Design” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mehndi usually hope their child will grow to embody henna design and live with faith, good character and purpose.

During this ceremony, the bride's hands and feet are adorned with intricate patterns of henna. This ritual is believed to bring good luck and prosperity to the newlyweds, emphasizing the importance of beauty and love in the marriage..
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic culture, the Mehndi ritual also has deep spiritual significance. Henna, a natural dye, is used as a reminder of the temporary nature of this world and the eternal beauty of the next world. This ritual is a reminder for the bride and her family that the permanent bond of marriage is grounded in faith and spiritual commitment, not just physical beauty. It also symbolizes the protection and blessings of Allah, as the design can last up to a week, making the bride feel cherished and shielded.
